newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa Telkom privatisation shortlist delayed.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa Telkom privatisation shortlist delayed.

text.p: The announcement of a shortlist of potential equity partners for South African state utility Telkom has been delayed but the list should be published in two to three weeks, a government spokesman said on Monday.
Posts and Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo had been expected to list three or four favoured partners last week or early this week.
But a spokesman for Naidoo said the news had been delayed. He gave no further details.
Eight international telecommunications groups are in the running to acquire an equity stake of up to 30 percent in Telkom. They are:
- a Dutch and Swedish consortium of KPN and Telia
Naidoo said last month the South African government hoped to finalise the deal for partial privatisation of Telkom by March next year.
The long-awaited deal, expected to spearhead the government's privatisation drive, is being closely monitored by financial markets, eager to see concrete progress in the sale of state assets.

The South African government has undertaken to double the number of private telephones over the next five years from four million serving mainly white areas at present to eight million, with a much greater penetration in traditionally black areas.
The government said on Sunday that SBC Warburg had been appointed to advise South Africa's telecommunications ministry on proposed privatisation.
SBC Warburg is to advise on sectoral issues and will interact with Goldman Sachs International, adviser to Telkom.
HSBC Investment Bank was awarded the wider tender to advise the government on overall restructuring of state assets last month.
